key_insight: Rice frequency provides a low-cost, two-scale descriptor of welding arc voltage, with disturbance responses that reverse between approximately 10 and 50 ms window widths.
engineering_relevance: Short-Time Rice Frequency Analysis could support online GMA welding monitoring when combined with other signal features.
method: Calculate Rice frequency as the square root of the second-to-zeroth spectral moment ratio.
Apply sliding-window analysis to arc voltage signals at different time scales.
Compare annotated disturbed and undisturbed segments within each weld to reduce session effects.
evidence_signal: Of 89 controlled welds, 80 were analysed; within-weld mean Rice frequency fell 24.5% under shielding gas interruption (5/5 welds) and rose 155% with a 16% current increase (7/7 welds).
watch_item: Window width changes response direction, while whole-weld pooling can dilute local disturbances; travel speed and localised oil contamination showed no consistent effect.
paper_title: A voltage signal analysis method for the welding process using the rice frequency
